components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
口 (mouth) — 吃 relates to eating, done with the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a sound close to 吃's reading chī
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
忄 (heart) — 惊 relates to an emotional reaction of shock or fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惊's reading jīng
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.
匕 (a person), doubled and mirrored — two people standing back-to-back; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional meaning 'north.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
礻 (spirit, altar) — 礼 relates to ceremony and rites performed before the spirits.
乚 reflects the character's phonetic root, though its exact link to the modern reading lǐ is unclear today.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'
心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
木 (wood) — 棍 names an object made of wood, a stick.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound close to gùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
大 (a person) at the top represents someone leading.
冖 (a rope or cover shape) in the middle shows a tether.
牛 (ox) at the bottom is the animal being led, giving 牵 its meaning 'to lead by hand, to pull.'
氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'
段 shows 殳 (a hand wielding a tool) cutting or shaping stone into pieces — giving 段 its meaning 'section, segment, paragraph.'
氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
心 (heart) — 怒 relates to strong feeling in the heart: anger.
奴 (nú) gives a sound close to nù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
氵 (water) — 洋 refers to the vast ocean
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 洋's reading yáng
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
层 depicts a roof-like covering stacked over what lies beneath, evoking one layer piled upon another.

meanings: younger male cousin through a female relative

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
虫 (worm, insect) — 蠢 originally described the wriggling movement of insects.
春 (chūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 蠢, differing only in tone.
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ
囗 (an enclosure) — something firmly closed in is secure, tied to 固's meaning 'solid, firm.'
古 (gǔ) gives a rhyme close to gù, with the tone shifted.
扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand
文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) gives a sound hint — 影 is pronounced yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.
冫 (ice) — 冷 relates to the cold of ice
令 (lìng) gives a sound close to 冷's reading lěng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
Wine — the original sense described the strong taste of wine.
Gives the sound gào, related to kù but drifted apart over time.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
广 (shelter) suggests a piece of furniture kept indoors.
木 (wood) — early beds were built from wood, giving 床 its meaning.
阝 (mound, place) shows 陪 relates to being present alongside someone somewhere.
咅 gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.
宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
目 (eye) — 睁 describes an action of the eyes.
争 (zhēng) gives the sound — an exact match for 睁.
目 (eye) — 睁 describes an action of the eyes.
争 (zhēng) gives the sound — an exact match for 睁.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'
穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi
扌 (hand) — 掘 describes digging with the hands or a tool.
屈 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 掘's reading jué, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.

圣 is the simplified form of 聖, which combined an ear (耳, listening) and a mouth (口, speaking) above a standing figure — the image of someone who listens and speaks with special insight, giving 圣 its meaning 'holy, sacred.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
哥 doubles the character 可 ('to approve, to sing'), originally suggesting a call-and-response song between two singers; the meaning later narrowed to 'elder brother.'
皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl
丿 — a single drop of blood inside the vessel
⺼ (flesh/meat) — 腥 describes the strong smell of raw meat or fish.
星 (xīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 腥.
癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'

meanings: (of a device, connection, material etc) defective

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

meanings: variant of 座標|坐标[zuo4 biao1]

components.note: 从 (two people, one following another) — depicts people together.
土 (earth/ground) — two people seated on the ground gave 坐 its meaning 'to sit.'
木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
Flesh — skin is part of the body.
Gives the sound fū, matching the character's reading.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
艹 (grass/plant) — 苏 relates to certain aromatic plants and to reviving, coming back to life
稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
